details: India has one of the largest road networks globally (approx 5.6 million km).
Road Network Classification: Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways (Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai-Mumbai), National Highways (NHAI), State Highways (PWD), District Roads, Border Roads (BRO).
Advantages: Lower construction capital, flexible terrain handling, door-to-door delivery, feeder network to rail and ports.
evidence_or_examples: North-South Corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) and East-West Corridor (Silchar to Porbandar).

details: Railways: Primary mode for heavy long-distance freight and passenger transit; network affected by terrain (dense in Northern Plains, sparse in Himalayas).
Pipelines: Modern transport for crude oil, petroleum, and natural gas; zero transit delays/losses (e.g., HVJ pipeline).
Inland Waterways: National Waterways (NW-1 Ganga between Allahabad and Haldia, NW-2 Brahmaputra between Sadiya and Dhubri).

Major Seaports: 12 Major and 200 notified non-major ports. Western Coast (Kandla/Deendayal, Mumbai, Marmagao, Mangaluru, Kochi); Eastern Coast (Tuticorin, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Haldia, Kolkata).
evidence_or_examples: Deendayal/Kandla tidal port developed post-1947 to relieve Mumbai port; Marmagao handling 50% iron ore exports.

sub_branches.concept: Mass Media, Digital Networks & Trade Balance
details: Personal & Mass Communication: Indian Postal Network (First Class mail: cards/envelopes; Second Class mail: book packets/newspapers), Telecom & Digital India, Doordarshan, Akashvani.
International Trade & Balance of Trade: Export vs Import monetary value. Favorable trade balance when exports > imports; Unfavorable when imports > exports.
Tourism as Invisible Trade: Earmarks massive foreign exchange, supports 15 million direct jobs, promotes national integration and cultural heritage.
evidence_or_examples: Foreign tourist arrivals spending foreign exchange directly on Indian hospitality, handicrafts, and heritage.
